hook: Siddhartha Srinivasa is a roboticist who describes himself as a full-stack roboticist, working across machine learning, perception, planning, and control. He spent eighteen years at Carnegie Mellon University's Robotics Institute, where in 2005 he founded the Personal Robotics Lab and developed robots including HERB and ADA, and contributed algorithms later used on NASA's Robonaut and on Mars rovers. From 2014 to 2017 he was a first-wave founder at the robotics automation startup Berkshire Grey. In 2017 he joined the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering as a professor, continuing his Personal Robotics Lab research there. The following year he also took on starting and leading Amazon's Robotics AI organization, growing it to roughly four hundred people, before later serving as a Distinguished Engineer at Cruise. He is a Fellow of IEEE for his contributions to robotic manipulation and human-robot interaction, and helped write the Roadmap for US Robotics presented to Congress in 2013.

standing.record: The site's records add up to a career pattern of founding and leading robotics groups, first in academia and then in industry. The Personal Robotics Lab at Carnegie Mellon, founded in 2005, produced HERB, ADA, CHIMP, and MuSHR, and his algorithms were later used on NASA's Robonaut and on Mars rovers, which places his work inside government and space robotics as well as consumer and warehouse automation. Berkshire Grey, founded in 2013, is the startup where he was a first-wave founder from 2014 to 2017, and Amazon is the public company where the site records him as an executive. He also helped write the Roadmap for US Robotics presented to Congress in 2013, tying his record to national research policy. The litigation the site holds is thin and indirect: two entries for Amazon.com Services, LLC v. Perplexity AI, Inc., and one for Haugland v. Anthropic PBC, none of which the records show naming him personally. The pattern that runs through the coverage is organizational building, with legal exposure appearing only through Amazon, a company he is recorded as an executive of.
